meta.source: Computed by npm run build:data from data/safety.json (element ratings) with assets/js/formulas.js
meta.notes: Resistance = volts² ÷ watts, formulas.elementResistanceOhms; current = watts ÷ volts, formulas.electricAmps. These are the cold readings of a good element at its rated voltage; A. O. Smith's own pass range is wider (5–25 ohms) to cover tolerance and other ratings.

ohms.caption: What a good heating element should read (cold, power off)
ohms.source: Ohm's law: resistance = volts² ÷ watts, current = watts ÷ volts (formulas.elementResistanceOhms, electricAmps). Element ratings sold for residential water heaters (The Home Depot listings, 2026-11-13); the right one for your heater is the voltage and wattage on its data plate (A. O. Smith). A. O. Smith's pass range: 5–25 ohms.
